overview.title: What is Plumia?
overview.text: Plumia is a global policy think tank exploring the future of citizenship and borders, with fellowships, cohorts, and an annual summit in Morocco.

overview.title: Who joins Plumia?
overview.text: Plumia draws together policymakers, researchers, founders, investors, and digital nomads working to reimagine global mobility. The community spans technologists, government officials, journalists, and academics united by interest in network states, nomad policy, and the future of citizenship.

overview.title: Plumia's Four Programs
overview.text: Plumia runs four core programs: the free weekly [Borderless newsletter](https://plumia.org/borderless/) (65,000+ subscribers), the [Internet Country Cohort](https://www.plumia.org/cohorts/) (a free virtual learning program), the [Plumia Fellowship](https://www.plumia.org/the-plumia-fellowship-2025/) (a three-month funded research grant), and the [annual Connect Summit](https://www.plumia.org/connect-summit/) in Essaouira, Morocco. Each program bridges policy thinking with the practical realities of borderless living.

history.text:
Plumia grew out of a hackathon at SafetyWing, a Y Combinator-backed company founded in 2018 by three Norwegian digital nomads building a global social safety net. The idea of an internet-native country offering portable citizenship, health insurance, and dispute resolution took shape internally before Plumia was publicly launched as an independent nonprofit in 2022.

Lauren Razavi, a British-Iranian political scientist and author of Global Natives, became the organization's Executive Director. Under her leadership, Plumia launched its first [Internet Country Cohort](https://www.plumia.org/internet-country-cohort/) in November 2022, bringing together curious and ambitious people to explore network states and digital governance through workshops and working groups.

In 2024, Plumia held its first [Connect Summit](https://www.plumia.org/connect-summit/) in Essaouira, Morocco, gathering nearly 100 researchers, policymakers, investors, and founders for a two-day working summit on global mobility. That same year, the Borderless newsletter grew from 2,000 to over 65,000 readers, cementing Plumia's standing as a leading voice in the digital nomad policy space.

The 2025 Plumia Fellowship - the organization's first funded research program - supported two fellows: Xiangyu Long, a doctoral researcher at Oxford studying emergent communities and blockchain, and Madison Karas, a product manager researching tax models for digital nations.

location:
Plumia operates as a virtual organization with its main in-person home in Essaouira, Morocco, where it hosts the annual Connect Summit each spring. Essaouira is a historic Atlantic port city whose UNESCO-listed medina has served as a crossroads of trade, culture, and ideas for centuries - a fitting home for a summit on borderless futures.

Plumia has no fixed headquarters and is funded by SafetyWing, whose team is globally distributed. The organization works in partnership with the City of Essaouira, the United Nations, and Interintellect.
duration:
Plumia offers several ways to engage, each with a different time commitment.

The [Borderless newsletter](https://plumia.org/borderless/) arrives weekly and requires no minimum commitment. The Internet Country Cohort runs for 4-6 weeks at roughly 2 hours per week, making it accessible for people with busy schedules. The Plumia Fellowship is a three-month funded program for researchers, thinkers, and artists. The Connect Summit is a two-day annual gathering in Essaouira each spring.
pricing:
Plumia's core programs are free to participate in. The [Borderless newsletter](https://plumia.org/borderless/) is a free weekly publication on Substack. Internet Country Cohorts are completely free to join. The Plumia Fellowship provides funding to fellows at no cost to applicants.

The annual Connect Summit in Essaouira is invitation-only; ticket pricing, if any, is not published publicly. Prospective attendees can submit an expression of interest through the [application form on the summit page](https://www.plumia.org/connect-summit/).

fellowship: The Plumia Fellowship is a three-month funded program supporting visionary thinkers, artists, and researchers reimagining the foundations of digital civilization. Fellows receive funding, mentorship, and global visibility while producing original work on citizenship, governance, and belonging in borderless contexts. The 2025 cohort - the first - supported two fellows: Xiangyu Long, a doctoral researcher at Oxford studying emergent communities and blockchain, and Madison Karas, a product manager researching tax models for digital nations. Applications for the 2026 fellowship are expected to open in mid-2026; subscribe to Borderless for updates.

howToEnter.text:
The easiest first step is subscribing to the free [Borderless newsletter](https://plumia.org/borderless/), which announces new cohorts, fellowship calls, and summit invitations as they open.

Internet Country Cohorts are the main open-access community program, running periodically and accepting applications through a form on the [cohorts page](https://www.plumia.org/cohorts/). The Plumia Fellowship opens applications in mid-year; check the official site or newsletter for updates. Invitations to the annual Connect Summit in Essaouira are curated - prospective attendees can apply through the [Connect Summit page](https://www.plumia.org/connect-summit/).

faqs.question: What is Plumia?
faqs.answer: Plumia is a global policy think tank and nonprofit organization focused on the future of migration, citizenship, and borders. It runs a weekly newsletter, free virtual learning cohorts, a funded fellowship program, and an annual summit in Morocco for policymakers, researchers, and founders working on global mobility.

faqs.question: Is Plumia a physical place?
faqs.answer: Plumia is primarily a virtual organization. Its main in-person gathering is the annual Connect Summit, held each spring in Essaouira, Morocco. The organization has no fixed headquarters.

faqs.question: How do I join Plumia?
faqs.answer: Start by subscribing to the free [Borderless newsletter](https://plumia.org/borderless/). From there, you can [apply for the Internet Country Cohort](https://www.plumia.org/cohorts/) when applications open, submit for the Plumia Fellowship in mid-year, or request an invitation to the annual Connect Summit.

faqs.question: Is Plumia free to participate in?
faqs.answer: Yes - the Borderless newsletter, Internet Country Cohorts, and fellowship application are all free. The Connect Summit is invitation-only and does not publish ticket pricing publicly.

faqs.question: What is the Borderless newsletter?
faqs.answer: Borderless is Plumia's free weekly newsletter covering digital nomadism, global mobility policy, network states, and internet culture. It has grown to more than 65,000 subscribers worldwide. Subscribe for free at [plumia.org/borderless](https://plumia.org/borderless/).

faqs.question: What is the Internet Country Cohort?
faqs.answer: The Internet Country Cohort is a free 4-6 week virtual program for curious and ambitious people exploring network states and digital governance. It includes workshops, speaker sessions with founders of existing internet country projects, and working groups. Cohorts run periodically; [apply here](https://www.plumia.org/cohorts/).

faqs.question: What is the Plumia Fellowship?
faqs.answer: The Plumia Fellowship is a three-month funded program supporting researchers, artists, and thinkers who are reimagining citizenship and digital civilization. Fellows receive funding, mentorship, and global visibility for original work. The 2025 cohort had two fellows; applications for 2026 are expected to open in mid-2026. See the [fellowship page](https://www.plumia.org/the-plumia-fellowship-2025/) for details.

faqs.question: What is the Connect Summit?
faqs.answer: The Connect Summit is Plumia's annual invitation-only working summit held in Essaouira, Morocco. It brings together roughly 100 policymakers, researchers, investors, and founders for two days of panels, fireside chats, and cultural experiences focused on global mobility. Past editions ran in 2024 and 2025; a 2026 edition was scheduled for May 6-7, 2026.

faqs.question: Who leads Plumia?
faqs.answer: Lauren Razavi is Executive Director - a British-Iranian political scientist and author of Global Natives. The team also includes Stefan Heggelund (Diplomatic Lead, former Norwegian MP), Eman Zabi (Operations Lead), Abril Carli (Creative Lead), and Chance McAllister (Community Lead). See the full team at [plumia.org/team](https://www.plumia.org/team/).

faqs.question: Is Plumia connected to SafetyWing?
faqs.answer: Yes. Plumia was spun out of SafetyWing, a Y Combinator-backed company that provides health insurance for digital nomads. SafetyWing funds Plumia, but Plumia operates as an independent nonprofit with its own team and programs.

faqs.question: What is the Nomad Visa Global Standard?
faqs.answer: The Nomad Visa Global Standard is a policy framework developed by Plumia to establish consistent international standards for digital nomad visas. It responds to the rapid growth of nomad visa programs - from Estonia's first effort to over 60 countries offering such visas by 2024. Plumia works directly with governments to help make nomad visas as accessible as tourist visas. The policy paper is available on [SafetyWing's blog](https://safetywing.com/blog/plumia-nomad-visas-policy-paper/).

faqs.question: What is an internet country, and why does Plumia focus on it?
faqs.answer: An internet country is a governance structure organized around shared values and digital identity rather than physical territory. Plumia's long-term vision is to build a country on the internet that provides the functions of a nation-state - health insurance, income protection, pensions, and dispute resolution - in a portable, borderless format accessible regardless of where you were born.
